The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- for the injuries suffered by him in a road traffic accident dated 17.11.2021.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, On 17.11.2021 at about 06.00pm when the petitioner was going along with his friend Maruthi who was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-HZ-7147 Honda Shine Company as a pillion rider and when proceeding near SCCH - 25 3 MVC No.3887/2022 Rayaradoddi, after Sathanoor near Malavalli, Kanakapura Main Road, a Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AM-2696 came from opposite side in a rash and negligent manner with high speed with an intention to overtake the other vehicle, suddenly took a right and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said accident the rider of the vehicle Maruthi died on the spot and the petitioner sustained head injury, eye injury and injury to his leg.

3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident, public shifted him to Government Hospital, Kanakapura, provided first aid treatment and later he was referred to Victoria Hospital, Bangalore, admitted as an inpatient, underwent surgeries and treated conservatively.

Thereafter, he was bed ridden in his native place at Bellary and taken treatment in VIMS at Bellary for loss of Vision in left eye and he has completely lost the vision in left eye he is still under treatment and discharged with advice.
So far he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food and nourishment etc., SCCH - 25 4 MVC No.3887/2022
Before the accident he was working as a Laborer at Bangalore Diary i.e., (BAMUL) and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability, he is unable to continue his work.
The accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AM-2696.
The Jurisdictional Police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.202/2021 for the offences p/u/Sec.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.
Therefore, the 1 st respondent being the RC Owner and the 2 nd respondent being the Insurer of the said offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.

5. The objection of the respondent No.1.
SCCH - 25 5 MVC No.3887/2022 He has denied all the petition averments and stated that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle and the respondent No.1 stopped his vehicle and provided the petitioner with water and taking advantage of the said situation in collusion with police petitioner has filed false case against him.

He has stated that the Ramesh A vs Anand D on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26311835/
2
Lorry has valid FC, RC, Pollution Certificate and the driver had a valid DL.
He has further submitted that the petition is not maintainable for non joinder of owner and insurer of the motorcycle.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.
6. The objection of the respondent No.2.
It has denied all the averments made in the petition except admitting the issuance of policy in favour of the Respondent No.1 in respect of the Lorry bearing KA-01-AM- 2969.
It has contended that the Lorry Driver did not have a valid and effective DL and the Lorry did not have a valid Permit as on the date of accident.
The petition is also bad for non compliance of Sec.158(6) & 134(c) of MV Act.
The petition is SCCH - 25 6 MVC No.3887/2022 bad for non joinder of insurer and the RC owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-HZ-7147.
It has also contended that there was contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle to an extent of 70%.

It has also denied the age,
occupation and the manner of accident.
It has contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive, arbitrary and disproportionate.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.

7. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 17.11.2021 at about 06.00pm, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AM-2696 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries.?
2. Whether the Petitioner he is entitled for Compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award?
The Petitioner in order to prove his case has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.15.
He has also examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.16 & 17.
He has also examined Dr.Krishna Prasad A.H. as PW.3 and got marked Ex.P.18.

On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness but got marked the insurance policy as Ex.R.1.
9.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.

The counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied upon the following decisions:
2021 ACJ 1952 : Chandrakantbhai Vs. Sipahi J. Maheboobbhai and Ors.
10.

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-

3  Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,

sentences.text: Issue No.2:

In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per the final order,
 for the following:-
 SCCH - 25 8 MVC No.3887/2022  REASONS  11. Issue No.1:-

In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AM-2696, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.8.
He has reiterated the contents of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
During the cross examination, he has denied all the suggestions made by the counsel for the Respondent No.2 about not wearing helmet and about the rider being negligent.
12. On perusal of the documents FIR at Ex.P.1 was registered on the next day of the accident on the complaint of the father of the deceased rider of the motorcycle.
The Mahazar at Ex.P.4 and the sketch at Ex.P.5 show that the Lorry came from opposite direction and suddenly took a right to the opposite side of the Road hitting the motorcycle.

Therefore, on perusal of sketch it is clear that there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and the SCCH - 25 9 MVC No.3887/2022 negligence was entirely on the part of the Lorry Diver.

The counsel for the respondent has contended that the Major damages are to the Two wheeler and the Lorry has suffered only simple damages that too only to the front bumper, radiator grill and front wind screen glass whereas, the motorcycle has suffered damages to its front wheel &
mudguard, head light and indicator assembly, handle bar, seat, crash guard, both side body shield and Tail lamp and indicator damaged as per Ex.P.6 IMV report.
However it is to be noted that in any accident the motorcycle gets entirely damaged, due to the impact.
But, only looking at the damages suffered by these Two vehicles, we cannot infer as to who is going in a high speed.
Ex.P.7 wound certificate shows that the petitioner suffered grievous injuries in an RTA dated 17.11.2021.
The police have conducted investigation and filed the charge sheet as per Ex.P.8 against the driver of the Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AM-2696.
In order to disprove the case of the petitioner, the respondents have not led any evidence.

SCCH - 25 10 MVC No.3887/2022 The counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied upon the following decision:
2021 ACJ 1952 : Chandrakantbhai Vs. Sipahi J. Maheboobbhai and Ors.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Gujarath has held that the contributory negligence of the Scooter to an extent of 30%.
Ramesh A vs Anand D on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26311835/
4

entities.text: Chandrakantbhai Vs. Sipahi J. Maheboobbhai and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However in this case it is seen that as per the sketch it appears that the entire negligence is of the driver of the offending Lorry Driver Therefore, there is no contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.

As such, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary relying on the documents at Ex.P.1 to 8, this court comes to the conclusion that the accident occurred on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AM-2696.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound SCCH - 25 11 MVC No.3887/2022 certificate as per Ex.P.7.
As per Ex.P.7, the Petitioner has suffered fracture to the femur and some injury to the brain and laceration to the left eyebrow which are grievous in nature.
14. In support of the same, the petitioner has also got examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.16 & 17 i.e., clinical notes and one X-ray.
He has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner and diagnosed to have closed right femur shaft fracture with pubic diastasis and head injury.

He further stated that the petitioner is suffering from total disability of the right lower limb at 47% and for the whole body physical disability at 16%.
15.
PW.2 in his cross examination has stated that he has not treated the petitioner.
He has assessed the disability of the petitioner only after 3 years of the accident.
He has also admitted that the injuries are healed and the fractures are united.
The Petitioner has also got examined Dr.Krishna Prasad A.H. an Opthomologist as PW.3 and got marked Ex.P.18 i.e., OPD slip.
He has assessed the disability of the petitioner with respect to his pale optic disc injury to the left eye.
He has fixed the disability of the left eye at 30%.
During his cross examination he has denied all the suggestions made by the counsel for the Respondent No.2.
He has stated that Exotropia means squint and RPAD means reaction of pupil to the light and Pl means perception of light.
The Respondent counsel has contended that the injuries to the eye is not connected to the RTA.
However, it is to be noted that in the discharge summary produced at Ex.P.9 relating to Victoria Hospital there was a followup of Opthomology and Neurology.
Thereafter it can also be seen that in VIMS Bellary Hospital the Doctors have noted that Suturing of the left eye was done after RTA.
But the petitioner has suffered loss of vision from about 2 months back i.e., from the date of accident itself.
Therefore, relying on all the medical documents and evidence of PW.3, this tribunal holds that the petitioner has lost vision SCCH - 25 13 MVC No.3887/2022 of left eye to an extent of 30%.

By using the telescopic formula, the total physical Ramesh A vs Anand D on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26311835/
5 disability of the petitioner comes to 40%.
Disability 17.

The Petitioner has stated that he was working as a Laborer at BAMUL, being Laborer the petitioner requires eye as well as leg because the Labor work is a manual work and requires physical capacity of the person.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the functional disability at 40%.

Monthly income:
18.
The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was working as a Labor at BAMUL and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
In this regard he has not examined any witness nor produced any documents like Bank statement etc., to prove his earnings.
The accident occurred in the year 2021.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.15,000/- per month.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 19 years as could be made out from SCCH - 25 14 MVC No.3887/2022 Ex.P.14/Aadhar Card.
He was hale and healthy before the accident.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:-

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Govt. Hospital, Kanakapura and thereafter Victoria Hospital, Bangalore wherein he was admitted and treated as an inpatient from 18.11.2021 to 02.12.2021 and was diagnosed and underwent surgery which can be made out from Ex.P.9.
Thereafter he was treated at VIMS Hospital, Bellary for loss of visions of left eye.

Considering that the nature of injury he has undergone is grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc.
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.12 for a sum of Rs.5,666/-.
There is no contrary evidence against these SCCH - 25 15 MVC No.3887/2022 bills from the Respondents.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under this head.

iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and lost his left eye vision.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary of Victoria Hospital to show the duration and treatment in the said hospital.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least One month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.15,000/- under this head.

Ramesh A vs Anand D on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26311835/
6 iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:-
On perusal of Ex.P.14, the petitioner's date of birth is mentioned as 12.06.2002 and the accident occurred on 17.11.2021.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 19 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 18.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of SCCH - 25 16 MVC No.3887/2022 Rs.12,96,500/- (Rs.15,000/- x 12 x 18 x 40%= Rs.12,96,000/-) under this head.

(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:-
The Petitioner was aged about 19 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained simple and grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 40% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.

Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered,
a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner SCCH - 25 17 MVC No.3887/2022 is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the version of PW.2, the Petitioner has to undergo another surgery for removal of implants and the estimation of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
In this regard neither the petitioner nor PW.2 has produced any estimation bill about further surgery.

As per the evidence of Pws.1 & 2 and looking at the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and the evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.

Therefore,
the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

19. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.1,00,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs.5,666/-
3. Loss of income during laid up period Rs.15,000/-

7

4 . Loss of future income Rs.12,96,500/-
 SCCH - 25 18 MVC No.3887/2022  5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/-
 happiness  6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/-
 nourishment charges

7 . Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000/-
 TOTAL Rs.14,77,166/-
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.14,77,200/- and same is awarded under to the Petitioner.
Liability 20.
The Respondents have contended that the driver of the Lorry did not have a valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
However, they have not proved their defence as discussed above.
Therefore, the Respondents being the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.1/insured and has to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.

The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.1,00,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of SCCH - 25 19 MVC No.3887/2022 Rs.14,77,200/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

Therefore,
the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
21. Issue No.4:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,77,200/- (Rupees Fourteen Lakhs Seventy Seven Thousand and Two Hundred only) along with interest at 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
SCCH - 25 20 MVC No.3887/2022 However, the Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
